rv.q: And that is exactly the feeling Birbiglia gives us at 'The New One.'
"The New One" is Birbiglia at his best – funny, thoughtful, and surprisingly touching.

On those terms, Mike Birbiglia‘s "The New One," transferred from a sold-out downtown engagement to a limited Broadway one, qualifies as a real play — a brimmingly warm, entertaining one on a universally relatable topic.
Merchant has a gift for finding the universal in the particular, and his show is both deeply personal and broadly accessible.
His unassuming demeanor is not part of the joke, but it does accentuate his humor, which is the opposite of unassuming or lazy.

But the biggest surprise is Birbiglia's ability to fill the stage with little more than the wit and wisdom of someone who understands that humor is the bitterest truth refusing to take itself seriously.
In that moment, we know he’s going to do all right as a father.
Not as big and spectacular as King Kong, needless to say, but gargantuanuously more entertaining.
Maybe because he’s able to laugh at the situation — and make everyone else laugh, too.
Running approximately 80 minutes, the show loses some steam as it goes along, trading bite for sentimentality and taking meandering turns, but overall it is very funny and well-constructed.
But this all serves to make him, well, boring.
The New One works out -- ingeniously.
In this time of political divide and tension, it was refreshing to laugh with an entire theatre of people about the troubles and aches of a universally human conundrum.
And while the material isn't exactly earth-shattering, it's always engaging and sometimes startling.
